exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean delivery)
outcome: maternal complications (need for blood transfusion, severe anemia, ICU admission)
cohort: Participants were patients presenting with retroplacental hematoma (RPH) and intrauterine fetal death (IUFD) at a single university hospital.
finding: The study found no statistically significant association between the diagnostic-to-expulsion interval and maternal complications, but low fibrinogen levels at admission were associated with an increased risk of severe hemorrhage and complications.
mod_finding: All cesarean deliveries resulted in complications (50% severe hemorrhage) compared to 21.7% of vaginal deliveries, and vaginal delivery was deemed feasible even in the presence of coagulopathies at admission.
